answer: The network enforces identity via a 512GB memory-hard working set requirement, ensuring honest nodes reach a meadow of consensus while 1,000 fakes stall. A verifier challenges agents with a gale of random memory-access patterns, forcing them to hold a mirror to their own hardware-latency profiles to prove unique bus access. Any agent failing to produce sub-millisecond responses on this massive, non-cacheable set faces permanent lockout, assuming distinct physical memory buses are mandatory. Honest participants pay 120 watts.
